domain_setting: A connected marine natural-history world spanning open ocean, shallow reef, rocky shore, kelp bed, and polar water. Keep sea life in water or on an appropriate shore; show aquarium entries as a public viewing habitat rather than a fishbowl.

ambient_palette.surface_sky: mist blue fading to warm ivory
ambient_palette.open_water: blue teal with deeper navy below
ambient_palette.reef_and_kelp: sea-glass green, muted kelp, and warm rock
ambient_palette.marine_animals: species-specific natural charcoal, blue-grey, silver, coral, and cream

recurring_scale_anchors: A thin waterline with small wave marks for surface swimmers and breaching animals
Bubbles and suspended particles for underwater depth
A few kelp blades, coral heads, or rock shapes for habitat and scale
A faint seabed or distant horizon to separate open water from the reef

polysemy_resolution_table.whale: The general marine mammal; avoid the throat grooves of a blue whale, long humpback flippers, or the square sperm-whale head so the species cards stay distinct.
polysemy_resolution_table.blue whale: An immense, streamlined blue-grey whale with fine ventral throat pleats and a small dorsal fin set far back; no humpback-length pectoral flippers.
polysemy_resolution_table.humpback whale: A robust whale with very long pectoral flippers, a small knobbly head, and a low hump near the dorsal fin.
polysemy_resolution_table.sperm whale: A deep-diving whale with an unmistakable large square block-shaped head and narrow lower jaw.
polysemy_resolution_table.killer whale: An orca with a black back, white eye patch and belly, and tall dorsal fin; it remains a dolphin-family mammal, not a fish.
polysemy_resolution_table.dolphin: A streamlined dolphin with a distinct long beak, curved dorsal fin, and playful surface leap.
polysemy_resolution_table.porpoise: A compact porpoise with a blunt rounded snout and short triangular dorsal fin; do not give it the dolphin's long beak.
polysemy_resolution_table.sea lion: A sea lion with visible external ear flaps and large front flippers, upright on a rocky shore.
polysemy_resolution_table.seal: A true seal with no external ear flaps, short fore-flippers, and a rounded resting body at the water's edge.
polysemy_resolution_table.walrus: An Arctic pinniped with two unmistakable long ivory tusks, whiskers, and a broad muzzle.
polysemy_resolution_table.otter: A small sea otter floating on its back with paws near its chest; distinguish it from a seal by its visible paws and fur.
polysemy_resolution_table.ray: The fish in this chapter is a flattened ray such as a stingray or manta, not a beam of light.
polysemy_resolution_table.school of fish: Several similar small fish swim tightly together in the same direction as one coordinated school.
polysemy_resolution_table.shrimp: A live small crustacean with a curled segmented body, long antennae, and swimmerets; not a plated food serving.
polysemy_resolution_table.squid: An elongated mantle with triangular side fins, eight shorter arms, and two distinctly longer feeding tentacles; distinguish it from the round-headed octopus.
polysemy_resolution_table.starfish: A sea star with five broad radiating arms resting on the reef; it is not a fish.
polysemy_resolution_table.scale (fish): A single reflective fish scale or patch of scales, not a weighing device or a balance.
polysemy_resolution_table.fin: A fish fin stays attached to the body and uses visible rays or a fan shape; do not use a bird wing.
polysemy_resolution_table.gill: Show the feathery respiratory gill structure beneath a fish's gill cover, not human lungs.
polysemy_resolution_table.claw(s): A jointed marine-crab or lobster claw shown attached to its animal, not a mammal paw or bird talons.
polysemy_resolution_table.shell: A ridged marine shell, preferably with a living clam or mollusk context; do not show a plated shellfish meal.
polysemy_resolution_table.anemone: A sea anemone with a central mouth and radiating soft tentacles attached to a submerged rock; not a terrestrial flower.
polysemy_resolution_table.aquarium: A public aquarium viewing tank with glass, marine exhibits, and a visitor scale cue; not a round home fishbowl.
polysemy_resolution_table.ocean: The vast open body of salt water reaching a distant horizon, with no nearby shore dominating the scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.reef: A shallow submerged reef habitat with coral structure and marine life; distinguish the underwater reef from the broad open ocean.

existing_asset_triage.lesson_57: No chapter-local SVGs existed before this pass. Five exact-term candidates from other lessons are clear and retained; the aquarium scene is structurally regrouped while preserving its recognizable exhibit artwork.

reviewed_candidates.reason: The shore crab has a clear domed carapace, raised paired claws, and jointed legs; it already uses the current five-layer format and suits the coastal setting.
The ridged seashell silhouette is immediately recognizable and already meets the current layered SVG format.
The broad open-water horizon directly teaches ocean and avoids the sailboat-focused framing of the other older ocean card.
The large marine mammal, horizontal tail flukes, side fin, and blowhole spray clearly read as a whale; its prompt is generalized for this chapter.

The public viewing tank, marine exhibits, glass frame, and visitor silhouettes clearly teach aquarium; the old source lacked the current layer groups, so its existing composition is retained and organized into the five required layers.
A goldfish in a small home bowl points to a pet fish and overlaps the aquarium idea; the chapter teaches wild and marine fish.
The close-up is a mammal paw claw scratching wood, not a crab or lobster claw.
These older market/food cards present sea animals or seafood on trays and counters rather than in the live marine habitats used by this chapter.
The sailboat makes the card about sailing or a day at sea; the clearer 52/ocean open-horizon illustration is retained instead.
